calls.head: Turnovers could swing this one
calls.body: The Islanders give up more dangerous chances after losing the puck than most, and the Blackhawks pounce.
calls.call: The Blackhawks get at least their usual 7.6% of their 5-on-5 chances right after winning the puck.
calls.nums: Chicago 8th for chances off turnovers (7.6% of their chances come right after winning the puck) · NY Islanders 31st for avoiding breakdowns
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 4 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: 4.2% of Chicago’s 5-on-5 chances came right after winning the puck, against their usual 7.6%.

calls.head: Depth against star power
calls.body: The Islanders are one of the league’s best for depth, at the deep end; the Blackhawks are near the bottom of the league, at the top-heavy end. Expect that gap to show.
calls.call: The Islanders spread their forward ice time deeper down the lineup than the Blackhawks.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 4 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: On bottom-six share of forward ice time, NY Islanders had 47% and Chicago 42%. Coming in, NY Islanders was at 44% and Chicago at 41%.
calls.beyond: NY Islanders’s bottom-six forwards played 47% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 44% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 8 games.

NYI.head: We had this close to even (59% for NY Islanders), and NY Islanders came through.

CHI.head: We had this close to even (41% for Chicago), and it went NY Islanders’s way.

surprises.head: Chicago tried a different line
surprises.body: A. Frondell, R. Kantserov, T. Bertuzzi played 12:05 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Chicago’s usual lines.

surprises.head: NY Islanders got the good looks
surprises.body: NY Islanders’s shots at 5-on-5 were more dangerous than usual: an 8.2% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.3% (league average 6.4%). A team strays this far about once every 10 games.

story.head: The Islanders beat the Blackhawks
paras: Bo Horvat scored twice, opening the scoring late in the first.
The chances were closer than the score. The Blackhawks tried a line they hadn’t used before: Anton Frondell, Roman Kantserov and Tyler Bertuzzi.

items.text: Whether the Blackhawks keep that line together at home against Carolina on Saturday.
One of the preview’s two calls held.
